text: To prove that a property P holds for every element of an inductively defined type (e.g. lists or binary trees) by structural induction, what must you show?
choices: Only that P holds for the largest element
That P holds for one example of each type
That P holds for each constructor, assuming P for the immediate sub-components (the inductive hypothesis)
That the type is finite, then check every element
explanation: Structural induction proves P for each constructor case (e.g. leaf/node, nil/cons), assuming P for the substructures used to build the element. There is no 'largest element,' one example per type is not a proof, and inductive types are generally infinite, so exhaustive checking is impossible.
